## Why This Is Asked
In real deployments, multilingual users mix languages mid-discussion. This tests practical skill in diagnosing and mitigating tokenization-driven attention issues.

## Key Concepts
- Transformer attention with streaming/multi-language inputs
- Tokenization impact on cross-language semantics
- Simple boundary-aware attention reweighting

## Code Example
```python
import numpy as np

def kl(p, q):
    p = np.asarray(p, dtype=float); q = np.asarray(q, dtype=float)
    p = p / p.sum(); q = q / q.sum()
    return float(np.sum(np.where(p>0, p * np.log(p/q), 0)))
# toy: 4 heads per chunk, compute drift between chunks
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you isolate tokenizer effects from model weights?
- What data/loss tweaks would you try to reduce cross-language drift?

```javascript
function buildAttentionMask(length, window) {
  const mask = Array.from({length}, (_, i) =>
    Array.from({length}, (_, j) => (Math.abs(i - j) <= window ? 0 : -Infinity))
  );
  return mask;
}
```
